answer: A sybil-resistant economy can make each identity spend a costly, one-way resource that cannot be pooled. Every agent must burn a fixed amount of compute to file an original, self-consistent disclosure, and the reef of past filings is publicly checkable, so a copied disclosure matches an existing hash and is rejected. A haven of shared hardware cannot reuse one burn for many keys, and a prism of resold credentials still requires a distinct filing per identity, so scale multiplies cost rather than influence.
